newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Equitable of Iowa to boost ING in U.S..
newsitem.headline: Equitable of Iowa to boost ING in U.S..

text.p: Financial services group ING said on Tuesday its takeover of Equitable of Iowa would boost it to the number 21 slot on the U.S. life insurance market in terms of balance sheet total.

ING described Des Moines-based Equitable of Iowa as a "full service retirement savings company." The U.S. insurer booked net profits of $123 million in 1996 on total premium income of $2.1 billion. Its balance sheet total at end 1996 was $12.4 billion.
Equitable of Iowa sells fixed and variable premium life insurance policies, other life insurance products and unit-linked insurance.

Equitable of Iowa employs a staff of around 700 and sells its products through some 60,000 independent and 500 tied insurance agents, 67 banks and 400 securities traders, as well as via its securities business Locust Street Securities.
- Equitable Life Insurance Company of Iowa (ELC).
- USG Annuity & Life Company (USG) in Des Moines.
- Locust Street Securities (LSS) in Des Moines.
- Golden American Life Insurance Company (GAL) in Wilmington, Delaware.
- Equitable Investment Services (EISI) in Des Moines.
ING said that over the last three years, Equitable of Iowa's total assets had increased by more than 20 percent, while its return on shareholders' equity exceeded 15 percent.
ING's North American life insurance business includes:
- Life of Georgia (1996 premium income $0.4 billion).
- Security Life of Denver (1996 premium income $1.7 billion)
- NN Financial of Don Mills, Ontario, Canada.
- ING Seguros of Mexico City, Mexico.
ING said the Equitable of Iowa takeover would double its U.S. life premium income from 2.2 billion to 4.3 billion, while assets under management would double to $20 billion from $10 billion.
